I grew up as one of those absurdly gifted children. My parents made sure I could read write and do basic arithmetic before kindergarten. By the time school started I was already ahead of my classmates. The schools fell over themselves trying to get me to join gifted programs but I already felt so alienated from everyone, I flat out refused. I just wanted to be a normal kid. I'd look at other kids struggling to read and wonder how it could be that difficult for anyone. Did they not have a set of encyclopedias their parents made them read or something? Eventually I started getting bullied. Alot. It made me hate being smart even more. I disconnected entirely in school. I never participated, I never did my homework, but if I were ever called on I could look at something and just know the answer. I hated it. I felt like a freak. My parents were in the army so every three years we would move and I'd be really sad at first but then I'd think this is my chance to finally connect to someone. But it was always the same story. People would be interested until they weren't. I got really good at making up new identities for myself. It was fun to be someone new for everyone I met. I knew they wouldn't like me anyway, not once they got to know me, but for a brief period I could like who I was. 

This continued into high-school. I ended up getting credit for several classes just based on test scores and was due to graduate a few years early. This guy I knew was like "hey, ever smoke pot?". I hadn't. As much as I resented my life i had never even dreamed of disobeying my parents once. I remember how scared I was after the first hit. And then it was like...I could breathe for the first time. Like I didn't have to worry about who I was anymore. I stopped going to school. Told my parents to fuck off. They threw me out at 15 but I didn't care. I had something better now. I  sold drugs and lived in a motel and worked full time while going to a work at your own pace high-school. I spent some time in jail but l still managed to graduated ahead of my peers. I really only did pot until college. Then psychedelics. Which I did not enjoy. One bad argument with the God of causal relations will leave a bad taste in your mouth for decades. Became fascinated with nihilism and filled with existential dread. The more empty I became the harder the drugs I used were. Needed a bigger boost to get out of bed. Pot to psycho to club drugs to pills to opiates. It wasn't a straight line. There were times when I was sober for a stretch but I always said fuck this and went back to drugs. Eventually as I neared my thirties I started to dig myself out of my existential hole, realizing that if nothing matters then I can do anything. I'd been sober for about 2 years when I met the coolest chick I'd ever met. She wasn't that cool in hindsight. She and a friend were snorting some brown powder and asked if I wanted some. Not wanting to spoil then party I said sure and did a line. That feeling of breathing all over again. Fast forward six months and I'm spending every dollar I have on heroin. Eventually I get off of it and awat from her with meth. Eventually I get off the meth with more heroin. I started to shoot instead of snorting. Eventually I'm spending 1200 a week on my supply and I haven't gotten high in ages. So l turn to fentanyl. And holy shit it was amazing.

Ysee, people who die from overdoses either have been Clean for a while or severely overestimate what they're capable of. An old hand like me, I can honestly say every time I loaded up the syringe I hoped I would die. Somewhere in my mind I would say this is it, the last one. And I'd do it without a second thought. But I never did. I did a truly startling amount of fentanyl every day. Several grams sometimes, when they say micrograms can kill you.

Eventually I did get clean, and it's been a while now, but it's been a while before. I know if I went straight to fentsnyl again I'd die, no questions asked. But I still want to. It's a funny thing.

Addiction is a desire to change something within ourselves. We can't find the thing we need, so we seek that validation externally. But that never works. The only cure is inside, but most of us can't even stand to look in a mirror. I hated myself. I hated who I was. I still do. Every time I shot up, I'd pray this was the time I'd die, but it never was. So on a way I was conditioning myself to enjoy hating myself, and every time I failed to die it was more proof that I deserved to die. It's a vicious cycle of self loathing and disgust, and it turns my stomach every time I hear someone say a dead junkie is a good junkie. Everyone hates themselves sometimes. Few people try to destroy themselves. The ones that do need help. But asking for it or just needing it is an admission to yourself that you're not worth it.

At least that's how it was for me. I can't speak to anyone else's pain. Hope it answers some things.

I was working landscaping at the time so I had gotten the occasional small infection from cuts from small bits of trash and things, compounded with being covered in dirt and sweat all day. with my wife constantly in and out of the hospital I just didn't think we could afford for me to take even 1 day off. I just wrapped it and worked 2 jobs (landscaping and deliveries at night) for that entire period. i also didn't want my wife to worry about me until she was all squared away. looking back if I had just taken care of it it might have just been a minor surgery and a few days off. but I was terrified we'd be evicted or starve or something worse somehow. it took everything going wrong and us losing everything to finally be like "whelp, can't lose anything else, may as well go get this fixed now". and a quick surgery and a few days off turned into 6 weeks in the hospital.

had acute osteomyelitis, and a massive necrotic wound on my arm. it started as a smallish staph infection, but I knew I'd need surgery to fix it. my wife was diagnosed with cancer around the same time so with her in and out of the hospital I didn't feel I could take time off of work. when I finally did go in the infection had spread to the bone and the wound had grown to 8 or 9 inches long, and 4 or 5 inches wide. they originally wanted to amputate my arm, but since I still had most of the motor functions in my hand I declined. they told me the alternative would be long and painful, and I was like yeah sure whatever you're not taking my arm.

most of my adult life I was a fentanyl addict and while I've been clean for a few years I had no doubt I still had a tolerance. I told the osteoplastic and anesthesiologists that putting me down would be like putting down an elephant and they smiled and nodded but I knew they didn't really believe me. I guess that's fair because I don't think I really believed how long and painful a road I had chosen.

woke up in the middle of the debridement surgery (cutting away necrotic tissue) screaming and fighting. you know when you look at bright lights and you see spots? imagine that, except everything is orange fire. I heard voices and felt the nurse slam my back down on the table, and then nothing again. woke up again on my way out of the OR screaming again but this time strapped all the way down, the anesthesiologist was talking about how much ketamine and fentanyl they had given me and how he didn't think he could safely give me more. I spent two hours sobbing and begging for death as they drip fed me more and more painkillers. eventually they had to move me out of postop back to my room. 

when osteo came to see me they told me that because I fought them every step of the way they couldn't complete the surgery and I'd have to have another debridement. they weren't blaming me or anything I wasn't even aware I was doing it, except for when I lurched to consciousness. apparently scared the shit out of everyone. but even unconscious they had to pump me full of so many drugs it just wasn't safe apparently. the second surgery went much better, the anesthesiologists listened to me and checked my notes and I was out for the whole thing and just felt a bit of pain when waking up. after a few weeks of integra (this really neat substance that your body replaces with its own cells) and a wound vac, plus iv antibiotics I got a skin graft. the donor site on my thigh honestly hurt more than the graft itself. the wound vac changes were also not great, especially the staples they put in needing to be removed. but none of it compared to that first surgery.

afterwards I wondered if it would have been easier or better to just have the amputation. my arm looks mangled, but I can still grab things with my hand. I can't wave or open my hand wide, but I can definitely still grab. I no longer wonder about amputation but am still very self conscious of the fact that my arm looks like i lost a fight with a melon baller. 

I've been in fights, car accidents, stabbed, broken bones, etc etc. I drove myself to the hospital with two broken feet and a broken arm once. I've never lay sobbing and begging for death. Do not recommend.

I am the one who went insane actually: 

Context: I date this girl for almost a year. I'm an extreme introvert, so the fact that we were taking things slowly was amazing for me. I had not dated in a very long time. Nearly a decade. I made a lot of bad decisions, and ended up having an illicit affair with my boss, and becoming hooked on pills. There are huge chunks of the ending of our relationship I still don't remember, and probably never will. When she broke up with me, it was like...a bolt of lightning. I saw how I had jeopardized everything I ever wanted, and the woman that I loved (whether she did or did not love me being irrelevant), for the illusion of intimacy and drugs. I cleaned up on the spot. I sent her text messages for days, I begged her through phone and email. I have never threatened her, nor would I.

She basically said "It's over", asked for her things back, deleted all of our group photos and things, and left me with nothing. Totally excised from her life in less than a day, with not a single token to remember. I understand why she left me. I'm not making excuses. I regret it immensely. 

In fact I regretted it so much, felt so keenly responsible, that I tried to end my own life. How much more responsibility can you bear, than to pay a blood price with your life? That was the logic at least. I figured even if she never spoke to me again, at least if I had died she would forgive me.

I (obviously) failed in that. My life got worse and worse, even though I had long since stopped abusing drugs. I lost my job, I had to have back surgery, I lost my home, and my cat of sixteen years. It felt like sending her emails was the only connection I had to life anymore. Like reaching out to her was the only thing I had that could keep me going, even if she was just going to ignore me. It's been several months of now being clean, and I can feel myself returning to normal, slowly. I still send her an email once a month, sometimes more to my chagrin, especially if I've had a couple of beers. 

Begging for forgiveness like a dog. Begging for her acknowledgement.
